cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the best fit between SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2 imagery in SWPC_CAT.

data.note: CME visible to the SW in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2 imagery. The potential source is likely beyond the west limb as seen from SDO AIA and STEREO A EUV imagery. The source may potentially be seen as faint moving field lines near the west limb in STEREO A EUV 195 imagery starting at 2026-07-20T04:05Z. A filament eruption centered around S15W10 as seen in SDO AIA 304 imagery starting at 2026-07-20T04:39Z was determined to not likely be the candidate source for this CME.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the best fit between SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2 imagery as well as the potential source location.

data.note: CME visible to the west in STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1 imagery. Not seen in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 in real-time due to a downlink data gap. The source is likely an eruption seen around S10W130 in STEREO A EUV 195/304 imagery starting at 2026-07-20T09:15Z with brightening, an ejecta of material, and post eruptive arcades. Former AR 14482, which rotated off of the Earth-facing disk on 2026-07-17, may be the potential source of this eruption based on EUV imagery. Moving field lines are also seen beyond the west limb in SDO AIA 193.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on source location as well as the best fit between GOES CCOR-1 and STEREO A COR2 imagery.

data.note: CME visible to the NE in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 imagery and to the NNE in STEREO A COR2 imagery. The source is likely a C1.6 flare as seen in SDO AIA 131 and an eruption starting at 2026-07-20T12:08Z with brightening and an ejecta of material best seen in GOES SUVI 304 imagery. This flare and eruption is associated with AR 14492 (approximately N15E65).

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the best fit between SOHO LASCO C2/C3, STEREO A COR2, and GOES CCOR-1 imagery in SWPC_CAT as well as the source location.

data.note: CME visible to the SW in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 and to the SSW in STEREO A COR2. The source is an eruption with a broad region of dimming best seen in STEREO A EUV 195 imagery extending from S30W80 to N15W100 starting at 2026-07-20T12:05Z. Moving/opening field lines are also seen in SDO AIA 171 in ISWA, SDO AIA 193, and GOES SUVI 284 imagery.

cmeAnalyses.note: Updated measurement with additional imagery based on the best fit between GOES CCOR-1, STEREO A COR2, and SOHO LASCO C3 imagery. This measurement focuses on tracking the leading edge of the majority of the material of the CME.
Preliminary measurement using early frames of imagery based on the best fit between STEREO A COR2, GOES CCOR-1, and SOHO LASCO C2/C3 imagery in SWPC_CAT as well as the source location.

data.note: Faint CME observed to the SW in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2, following bright CME: 2026-07-20T13:26Z. The source for this CME is not very clear in STEREO A EUV imagery, but may be a small moving of field lines seen in SDO AIA 171 over the SW limb starting around 2026-07-20T15:05Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Triangulation between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2.

data.note: Faint CME observed to the NW in SOHO LASCO C2 and STEREO A COR2. Not observed in SOHO LASCO C3 likely due to faintness and/or the pylon, and not in GOES CCOR-1 likely due to faintness. The source is likely former AR 14482 located approximately around S08W135, observed only in STEREO A EUVI 195 as brightening on the region and field line movement deflected northward starting around 2026-07-20T18:55Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Triangulation between SOHO LASCO C2 and STEREO A COR2.

data.note: Thin, faint CME observed to the NE in STEREO A COR2 only, likely due to the GOES CCOR-1 occulting disk and real-time SOHO LASCO C2/C3 downlink gap (but also may be blocked by its occulting disk). The source is likely AR 14493, associated with an M1.1 flare in SDO AIA 131 peaking at 2026-07-20T19:20Z, also observed as brightening and field line movement in SDO AIA 171/193 and field line movement in STEREO A EUVI 195 near its east limb around 2026-07-20T19:55Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: STEREO A COR2 only 3D analysis using the source longitude of E09 to approximate the measurement, as such parameters may vary slightly. Due to several poor quality running difference images, only 3 available frames are used for this analysis.

data.note: Faint CME observed to the NE in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2. The source for this CME is not clearly defined but supported by triangulation around N33E42. This may be observed an area of weak dimming centered around N15E35 starting around 2026-07-20T19:39Z in SDO AIA 193, following a from AR 14493 responsible for CME: 2026-07-20T19:53Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Triangulation between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2.

data.note: Faint CME observed to the W in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1. No clear source is observed for this CME, and is likely far-sided.

cmeAnalyses.note: SOHO LASCO C2/C3 plane-of-sky with the unseen, likely far-sided source, and no STEREO A COR2 to triangulate.

data.note: Very narrow (<10 degree half-width), jet-like CME first seen to the NE in SOHO LASCO C2 starting at 2026-07-21T22:12Z. It is also faintly seen in SOHO LASCO C3 and GOES CCOR-1. The source of this CME is possibly related to a small amount of ejecta seen over the NE limb in SDO AIA 304 around 2026-07-20T21:18Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Plane-of-sky measurement chosen due to lack of triangulation and beyond-limb source candidate.

data.note: Faint CME observed to the W in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 only. No clear source candidate is observed in SDO AIA or GOES SUVI.

cmeAnalyses.note: This is a SOHO LASCO C2/C3 plane-of-sky measurement.

data.note: CME first seen to the WNW in STEREO A COR2 starting at 2026-07-21T06:23Z. It is also seen to the NW in SOH0 LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 but is largely obscured by the pylon in SOHO LASCO C3 and GOES CCOR-1. There is a larger shock feature that appears as a halo in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1. The source of this CME is most likely wide opening field lines seen near the W limb in STEREO A EUVI 195 beginning around 2026-07-21T05:55Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement of brightest, densest part of the leading edge based on best fit among SOHO LASCO C2, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2.
Shock front triangulation between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2.

data.note: CME first seen to the NW in SOHO LASCO C2 starting at 2026-07-21T07:48Z. It also seen to the NW in SOHO LASCO C3 and GOES CCOR-1 and to the N in STEREO A COR2. The source of this CME is a filament eruption in the NW quadrant of the Earth-facing disk best seen in GOES SUVI 304 approximately centered around N45W60. The filament can be seen lifting off the disk as early as 2026-07-21T05:00Z. The filament eruption is followed by a wide-spread area of dimming best seen in SDO AIA 195. This CME follows and partially overlaps with the back of large, far-sided CME: 2026-07-21T06:23Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on best fit among SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2 and visible, on-disk source location.

data.note: This CME is visible to the northeast in STEREO A COR2 imagery, and is faint but may be seen to the northwest in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 imagery. The source may be related to an eruption/brightening from Active Region 14493 (N10W05) starting around 2026-07-21T12:00Z seen in SDO AIA 131/171/193/304, GOES SUVI 131/171/195/284/304, and STEREO A EUVI 195/304 imagery. There is a coronal hole north and south of this eruption site which may account for deflection from the on-disk source location.

cmeAnalyses.note: Speculative measurement based on the best fit between STEREO A COR2 and a faint leading edge seen in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 imagery. It is unclear if the feature visible in SOHO LASCO imagery is outflow or the same event that is seen clearly in STEREO A COR2 imagery.

data.note: Slow moving, possible streamer blowout CME to the SW in SOHO LASCO C2 (before data gap), GOES CCOR-1, and to the S in STEREO A COR2 imagery. The CME is currently not visible in SOHO LASCO C3 due to the on going expected data gap due to downlink schedule. The source may be associated with moving/opening field lines in the SW quadrant below a coronal hole and between the longitudes of roughly W20 to W45 and latitudes of roughly S40 to S50 as seen in SDO/AIA 193 starting around 2026-07-21T21:00Z. A dimming signature is also visible to the SW starting around 2026-07-22T01:28Z. There is an additional dimming and brightening starting around 2026-07-22T11:00Z further to the S in SDO/AIA 193. All of these dimming features are believed to be associated with the overall streamer blowout feature to the SW in SOHO LASCO C2.

cmeAnalyses.note: Preliminary measurement using GOES CCOR-1 and STEREO A COR2 frames. There is likely deflection within the field of view due to proximity of a coronal hole.

data.note: Very faint front first seen to the S in SOHO LASCO C2 starting around 2026-07-23T06:36Z. It is also seen to the S in SOHO LASCO C3 and GOES CCOR-1 and to the SSE in STEREO A COR2. There is some movement and brightening along a filament channel that was centered around S10W00 best seen in SDO AIA 193 starting around 2026-07-23T05:54Z. This would require some significant southward deflection, but that could be accounted for by the proximity to a coronal hole south of AR 14493.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on best fit among SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2. There is some degree of uncertainty in this measurement due to the faintness of the leading edge.

data.note: Faint, narrow (<10 degree half-width) CME first seen to the SW in SOHO LASCO C2 starting at 2026-07-23T10:36Z. It is also seen to the SW in SOHO LASCO C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2. A possible source candidate is some very minor field line movement from beyond the SW limb best seen in SDO AIA 193 as early as 2026-07-23T08:27Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on best fit among SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2.

data.note: CME first seen to the E in STEREO A COR2 starting at 2026-07-23T15:38Z. The CME is also visible to the east in SOHO LASCO C3, but not clearly visible in SOHO LASCO C2 or GOES CCOR-1 imagery due to it's faintness. The source is most likely related to a C2.7 flare from around S20E19. The flare and associated eruption is best seen in SDO AIA 131. Field line movement and a faint EUV wave can be seen in SDO AIA 193. The eruption appears to be directed northward.

cmeAnalyses.note: Parameters based on best fit of features seen in STEREO A COR2 and SOHO LASCO C3.

data.note: Faint CME visible to the NE in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and to the NW in STEREO A COR2. The source is likely a filament eruption visible beyond the NE limb in SDO/AIA 171 and GOES SUVI 304 and 284 starting around 2026-07-23T14:17Z. The source is also visible to the NW in STEREO A EUVI 304.

cmeAnalyses.note: Parameters based on best fit using SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery.

data.note: CME first seen to the SE in STEREO A COR2 starting around 2026-07-24T04:38Z. It is also seen to the S in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1. The source is a filament eruption centered around S20E15 best seen in SDO AIA 193 starting as early as 2026-07-24T04:04Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement of the brightest part of the leading edge based on best fit among SOHO LASCO C2/C3, STEREO A COR2, and GOES CCOR-1.
SHOCK measurement tracking the outermost faint feature, based on the best fit between SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2 imagery.

data.note: Wide CME with irregularly shaped leading edge first seen to the SE in SOHO LASCO C2 starting at 2026-7-24T12:48Z. It is also seen to the SE in GOES CCOR-1 and to the SW in STEREO A COR2. In real time, only the earliest frame in seen by SOHO LASCO C2 due to a real-time gap between downlinks. The source is most like a wide opening of field lines best seen beyond the SE limb in GOES SUVI 284 starting around 2026-07-24T12:24Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on best fit between GOES CCOR-1 and STEREO A COR2.

data.note: Faint CME observed to the SE in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2. The source is not directly clear but triangulates well to ~S26E65. Potential weak sources are field line movement over the SE limb in GOES SUVI 171 starting around 2026-07-24T20:20Z, a brightening and field line movement in SDO AIA 171 around ~S04E30 near AR 14494 starting around 2026-07-24T21:01Z (requiring large deflection), or a small brightening in SDO AIA 193 around ~S40E70 starting around 2026-07-24T21:12Z (although this starts right with the front visibility).

cmeAnalyses.note: Triangulation between GOES CCOR-1 and STEREO A COR2.

data.note: Faint, diffuse CME visible to the NE in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and possibly to the N in STEREO A COR2 imagery. This CME is not clearly visible in GOES CCOR-1 imagery. This CME is likely associated with moving/opening field lines visible beyond the NE limb in GOES SUVI 284 starting around 2026-07-24T23:00Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Parameters based on best fit using SOHO LASCO C2 and STEREO A COR2 frames.

data.note: Faint CME observed to the SW in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1. The source is likely a small brightening and field line movement in SDO AIA 171/193/304 centered around S28W50 starting around 2026-07-25T01:06Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: GOES CCOR-1 only 3D measurement using W50 as estimated source longitude, and parameters could vary slightly as a result.

data.note: Faint CME observed to the SE only in GOES CCOR-1. No distinct source for this CME is observed with three weak, faint eruptive candidates: field line movement over the E limb in GOES SUVI 171 around 2026-07-25T02:16Z, field line movement over the SSE limb in SDO AIA 171 starting around 2026-07-25T03:03Z, or a brightening south of AR 14494 around S20E35 starting around 2026-07-25T03:36Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: GOES CCOR-1 plane-of-sky.

data.note: Faint CME observed to the NW in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 before a data gap, and in GOES CCOR-1 very faintly. The source is likely AR 14493, with a swath of brightening in SDO AIA 193 starting around 2026-07-25T02:28Z centered ~N10W55, with the brightest and most eruptive activity (filament material jostles but poorly erupts if at all) centered ~N05W65.

cmeAnalyses.note: GOES CCOR-1 only 3D measurement using W65 as the source longitude, as such parameters may vary slightly.

data.note: Faint CME observed to the NE in only STEREO A COR2. The source may be an area of slow dimming centered around N50W30 in SDO AIA 193 starting around 2026-07-25T03:33Z, offset significantly from the start time due to a data gap in STEREO A COR2 not becoming available until 2026-07-25T07:23Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: STEREO A COR2 only 3D measurement using W30 as the approximate source, finding southward deflection (somewhat speculative due to the large deflection necessary here), as such parameters could vary.

data.note: Faint CME observed to the SE only in GOES CCOR-1. No distinct source for this CME is observed with two weak, faint eruptive candidates: field line movement over the E limb in SDO AIA 171 starting around 2026-07-25T05:29Z, or a brightening south of AR 14494 around S20E32 starting around 2026-07-25T05:56Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: GOES CCOR-1 plane-of-sky.

data.note: CME observed to the NW only in GOES CCOR-1, and no distinct source is observed for this CME. In close timing there is a snappy field line movement over the NW limb starting around 2026-07-25T12:36Z in SDO AIA 171/193, but this occurs after the CME is first visible in GOES CCOR-1 and is not a great association.

cmeAnalyses.note: GOES CCOR-1 plane-of-sky.

data.note: Faint CME observed to the SW in SOHO LASCO C2, very faintly in GOES CCOR-1 and LASCO C3, and likely not in STEREO A COR2. This CME has no clear observed source, and is analyzed to be separate from the source for CME: 2026-07-26T16:23Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: SOHO LASCO C2 only plane-of-sky as the best observing coronagraph, with the leading edge diffusing within the C2 field-of-view.

data.note: CME first seen to the E in STEREO A COR2 starting at 2026-07-26T16:23Z. It is not seen in GOES CCOR-1 and is covered by a real-time data gap in SOHO LASCO C2/C3. The source of this CME is likely associated with an impulsive M3.2 flare from AR 14494 (S05E03) that peaked at 2026-06-27T15:28Z. The flare is best seen in SDO AIA 131.

cmeAnalyses.note: Highly speculative measurement based on visible source location and three frames in STEREO A COR2. After the third frame, the COR2A imagery becomes too grainy to track the leading edge.

data.note: CME first seen to the NE in SOHO LASCO C2 starting at 2026-07-26T20:26Z. It is also seen to the NE in SOHO LASCO C3 and GOES CCOR-1 but is missed in real time by a data gap in STEREO A COR2. The source is like a wide opening of field lines from beyond the NE limb best seen in GOES SUVI 284 starting as early as 2026-07-26T18:44Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Updated, triangulated measurement including new imagery from STEREO A COR2.

Plane-of-sky measurement based on running difference imagery from SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1. Plane-of-sky measurement chosen due to far-sided source and lack of real-time STEREO A COR2 imagery.

data.note: CME observed to the NE in STEREO A COR2 and faintly in GOES CCOR-1, not in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 due to a real-time downlink gap. The source is a heavily deflected filament eruption observed well in GOES SUVI 304, from a small filament spanning approx. N16E12 to N25W00 (centered N25E05) at 2026-07-27T03:13Z when it began to slowly lift off, more fully lifting off past 2026-07-27T05:00Z, clearly deflecting sharply NE in the field-of-view. Field line movement and brightening in GOES SUVI 171 and dimming in GOES SUVI 195 was also observed.

cmeAnalyses.note: Triangulation between STEREO A COR2 and the faint leading edge in GOES CCOR-1.

data.note: CME observed to the NW in GOES CCOR-1 and STEREO A COR2, not yet in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 due to a downlink gap. The source is a filament eruption far-sided from Earth, observed first in GOES SUVI 304 as the filament eruption over the NW limb starting around 2026-07-27T05:13Z. STEREO A EUVI 195/304 also observes the eruption site after a data gap ends at 2026-07-27T07:05Z and 2026-07-27T07:15Z respectively, as dimming, double-ribbon flare, and post eruptive arcade centered approximately around N25W125.

cmeAnalyses.note: Triangulation between GOES CCOR-1 and STEREO A COR2.

data.note: CME visible to the NE in GOES CCOR-1 and STEREO A COR2 imagery. Not seen in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 imagery in real-time due to a data gap starting at 2026-07-27T06:48Z. The potential source is field line movement on or just beyond the NE limb as seen in SDO AIA 171 imagery in ISWA, SDO AIA 193, and GOES SUVI 284 starting around 2026-07-27T09:37Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the best fit between GOES CCOR-1 and STEREO A COR2 imagery in SWPC_CAT as well as potential source location near the east limb.

data.note: CME visible to the NNE in STEREO A COR2 imagery only. There is a downlink data gap in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 in real-time starting at 2026-07-27T06:48Z and the CME is likely obscured by the pylon in GOES CCOR-1 imagery. The potential source is an eruption with dimming seen centered around N45W40 starting as early as 2026-07-27T09:25Z. The eruption is best seen in the NE quadrant of STEREO A EUV 195 imagery and the NW quadrant of SDO AIA 193 imagery.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the potential source location using STEREO A COR2 imagery in SWPC_CAT.

data.note: Faint CME observed to the SW only in GOES CCOR-1, likely too faint or blocked by occulting disk in STEREO A COR2, and with a real-time data gap in SOHO LASCO C2/C3. The source is likely just south of AR 14491 (S11W79), as a brightening and field line movement centered ~S19W80 in SDO AIA 171/193/304 starting around 2026-07-27T13:28Z and STEREO A EUVI 195/304 starting around 2026-07-27T13:45Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: 3D GOES CCOR-1 only analysis using W80 as approximate longitude via SDO observations, and as such parameters may vary slightly.

data.note: This CME is visible to the northeast in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2 imagery. The source is likely related to eruptive activity from a currently unnumbered region centered near N12E80. Subsequent field line movement is visible over the northeast limb starting around 2026-07-27T14:00Z seen in SDO AIA 171 imagery.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the best fit between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery.

data.note: This CME is visible to the northeast in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2 imagery. The source is likely related to an eruption from a currently unnumbered region centered near N16E80 starting around 2026-07-27T14:30Z as seen in SDO AIA 171/193/304 imagery.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the approximate source location and best fit between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery.

data.note: This CME is visible to the northeast in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 imagery. This event is not seen in STEREO A COR2 imagery due to a data gap starting at 2026-07-27T16:23Z. The source is likely far-sided as there are no clear source signatures visible on the Earth-facing disk around the time of this event.

cmeAnalyses.note: A plane-of-sky measurement was made using a longitude of -90 degrees due to the far-sided and therefore unknown source location.

data.note: This CME is visible to the northeast in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2 imagery. The source is an eruption near the northeast limb centered near N20E90 starting around 2026-07-27T23:30Z as seen in SDO AIA 131/171/193/304 and GOES SUVI 131/171/195/284/304 imagery. A subsequent opening of field lines is visible over the northeast limb in SDO AIA 131/171/193 and GOES SUVI 171/195/284 imagery.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the approximate source location and best fit between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery.

data.note: This CME is visible to the southwest in SOHO LASCO C2 and STEREO A COR2 imagery. Not clearly visible in GOES CCOR-1 imagery. The source is a filament eruption from Active Region 14494 (centered near S04W16) starting around 2026-07-27T23:45Z as seen in SDO AIA 131/171/193/304, GOES SUVI 131/171/195/294/304, and STEREO A EUVI 195 imagery. This eruption is preceded by a C3.3 flare starting at 2026-07-27T22:44Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the approximate source location and best fit between SOHO LASCO C2 and STEREO A COR2 imagery.

data.note: CME visible to the NE in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 imagery. The CME may faintly be visible to the north of the NE streamer in STEREO A COR2 imagery. The potential source is not clear, but may be an eruption around N05E55 starting as early as 2026-07-27T23:00Z in SDO AIA 193 and GOES SUVI 284 imagery as moving field lines.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the best fit between SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and one frame of available STEREO A COR2 imagery in SWPC_CAT as well as the potential source location. Due to the uncertainty in the source location, there is higher uncertainty than usual in this measurement.

data.note: Narrow CME visible to the SW in SOHO LASCO C2/C3. Not clearly visible in GOES CCOR-1 or STEREO A COR2 imagery. The potential source may be an eruption starting at 2026-07-28T00:21Z at S10W60 as best seen in GOES SUVI 304 imagery. The eruption is also seen as dimming and moving field lines in STEREO A EUV 195 imagery.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on source location using SOHO LASCO C2/C3 imagery. The CME is likely narrower than 10 degrees half-width based on SOHO LASCO imagery.

data.note: CME seen to the NE in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1. The CME is also possibly seen faintly to the NE in STEREO A COR2 imagery, but partially obscured by the NE streamer. The potential source is an eruption starting at 2026-07-28T02:17Z best seen as dimming and moving field lines in SDO AIA 193 imagery. The eruption can also be seen in GOES SUVI 304 imagery.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the source location using SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 running difference imagery. The CME's leading edge was not clearly measurable in STEREO A COR2 imagery.

data.note: CME visible to the east in GOES CCOR-1 imagery. The CME is faintly visible to the east in STEREO A COR2 imagery. The CME is not seen in real-time in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 imagery due to a downlink data gap. The potential source may be an eruption west of AR 14498, at approximately N14E65, starting around 2026-07-28T11:27Z with dimming and moving field lines best seen in SDO AIA 193.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the best fit between GOES CCOR-1 and STEREO A COR2 imagery as well as the potential source location in SWPC_CAT.

data.note: CME visible to the NE in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2 imagery. The potential source is an eruption near AR 14498, approximately N15E55, with moving field lines starting around 2026-07-29T22:42Z as best seen in SDO AIA 193 imagery.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the best fit between SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2 imagery in SWPC_CAT as well as the potential source location.

data.note: CME visible to the east in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2. The potential source is an eruption centered around S10E35 with dimming, moving field lines, and a possible faint EUV wave best seen in SDO AIA 193 imagery starting at 2026-07-29T02:06Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the best fit between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery in SWPC_CAT, with possible slight deflection to the east of the source location.

data.note: This CME is visible to the north in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and to the northeast in STEREO A COR2 imagery. This event is not seen in GOES CCOR-1 as it is obscured by the pylon. The source may be related to a filament eruption centered near N35W05 which begins to slowly lift off around 2026-07-29T23:00Z as seen in SDO AIA 171/193/304, GOES SUVI 171/195/284/304, and STEREO A EUVI 195/304 imagery. Dimming is observed from the eruption site in SDO AIA 193 and GOES SUVI 195 imagery starting as early as 2026-07-29T21:00Z and an EUV wave is seen moving northeast of the eruption site from 2026-07-29T23:00Z to 2026-07-30T03:00Z, indicating northern deflection.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the approximate source location and best fit between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery.

data.note: CME observed as a NE halo in STEREO A COR2, and a NW halo in GOES CCOR-1 partially blocked by the pylon. SOHO LASCO C2/C3 not available in real-time due to a downlink gap, but observed as a NW halo here once imagery backfilled. The source is associated with an M1.9 flare from AR 14492 peaking at 2026-07-30T17:00Z, observed in SDO AIA 131. This eruption is also observed as filament ejecta in SDO AIA 304 first lifting as early as 2026-07-30T15:18Z, more eruptively after 2026-07-15:43Z. SDO AIA 171/193 observe brightening, dimming, field line movement, EUV wave, and post-eruptive arcades.

cmeAnalyses.note: Preliminary shock STEREO A COR2 only analysis.

Updated analysis with available SOHO LASCO C3 imagery, triangulated with STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1. This fit is just inside the furthest lobed bumps of the front, capturing the core of the brightest material.
Preliminary bulk STEREO A COR2 only analysis.
Triangulation between GOES CCOR-1 and STEREO A COR2 using the observed source location, noting eastward deflection.

data.note: CME first seen to the NW in SOHO LASCO C2 starting around 2026-07-30T23:37Z. It is also seen to the NW in SOHO LASCO C3 and GOES CCOR-1. There is a faint feature in STEREO A COR2 that could be associated, but the leading edge is not trackable in COR2A. This front is most likely outflow following CME: 2026-07-30T16:53Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Plane-of-sky measurement chosen due to lack of separate source candidate and because no leading edge could be tracked in STEREO A COR2.

data.note: CME first seen to the NW in SOHO LASCO C2 starting around 2026-07-31T02:24Z. It is also seen to the NW in SOHO LASCO C3 and GOES CCOR-1. There is a faint feature in STEREO A COR2 that could be associated, but the leading edge is not trackable in COR2A. This front is most likely outflow following CME: 2026-07-30T16:53Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Plane-of-sky measurement chosen due to lack of separate source candidate and because no leading edge could be tracked in STEREO A COR2.

data.note: CME first seen to the NNW in STEREO A COR2 starting at 2026-07-31T03:08Z. While there is not a definite source candidate, this feature could possibly be related to some post eruptive arcades centered around N00W135 seen in STA EUVI 195 and STA EUVI 304 SW of former AR 14493 beginning around 2026-07-31T03:05Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Speculative measurement based only on possible source location N00W135

data.note: Very faint feature first seen to the N in SOHO LASCO C2 starting around 2026-07-31T03:24Z. This feature may be seen to the NNE in STEREO A COR2, but the image quality is too poor to be sure. The majority of the CME is obscured by the pylon in both SOHO LASCO C3 and GOES CCOR-1. The source of this CME may be a filament eruption near the NW limb centered around N40-50W70-80 and best seen in SDO AIA 304 and SDO AIA 193. The filament starts to rise off the disk about 2026-07-31T00:30Z and "snaps" around 2026-07-31T02:00Z, but the majority of the associated material appears to fall back to the disk. Additionally, this CME may simply be outflow following CME: 2026-07-30T16:53Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Speculative measurement based only on limited SOHO LASCO C2 imagery and a filament eruption centered around N40-50W70-80 as a potential source.

data.note: CME first seen to the NW in STEREO A COR2 starting at 2026-07-31T08:08Z. It is also seen to the NE in GOES CCOR-1 but is covered by a real-time data gap in SOHO LASCO C2/C3. This is most likely outflow following CME: 2026-07-30T16:53Z. No additional source has been identified for this front.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on best fit between STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1.

data.note: Faint CME observed to the E in STEREO A COR2, and faintly to the W/NW in GOES CCOR-1. The source is likely an area of diffuse dimming centered ~S20W35, observed in SDO AIA 193 starting around 2026-07-31T12:54Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Triangulation between STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1.

data.note: Faint CME observed to the NE in SOHO LASCO C2, may be observed to the NE in GOES CCOR-1 but heavily obscured by overlapping far-sided CME: 2026-07-31T23:00Z and real-time data gaps. The source may be the cluster of AR 14498/14450, closer to AR 14498 as brightening near N15E29 surrounded by some weak dimming and field line movement in SDO AIA 193 starting around 2026-07-31T19:25Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: SOHO LASCO C2 only 3D analysis using the observed likely source longitude at E29. Front may be visible in GOES CCOR-1 but too muddled by far-sided CME: 2026-07-31T23:00Z to confirm.

data.note: CME observed to the NE in SOHO LASCO C2 until a data gap begins at 2026-07-31T23:24Z, GOES CCOR-1, and to the NW in STEREO A COR2 after a data gap ends at 2026-07-31T23:38Z. The source for this CME may not be clearly observed, with the only source candidate being on/near the SW limb in STEREO A EUVI, as field line movement around 2026-07-31T17:25Z in EUVI 195 and prominence brightening in EUVI 304 around 2026-07-31T18:45Z as a data gap begins. This source would be around approximately W156.2 with STEREO A at W66.2, and triangulation supports approximately E166, so would be far to be the source match. This CME front was originally analyzed to an on-disk source, updated to be far-sided with more coronagraph imagery available afterwards to triangulate.

cmeAnalyses.note: Triangulation between GOES CCOR-1 and STEREO A COR2 found the previously analyzed LE in SOHO LASCO C2 to fit this triangulation as well, pushing the source to be far-sided rather than the original on-disk source.
SOHO LASCO C2 only 3D analysis using the source longitude E29, as the best/only observing coronagraph so far.

data.note: Very faint, narrow (<10 degree half-width), jet-like CME first seen to the NE in GOES CCOR-1 starting at 2026-08-02T10:45Z. In real time, this CME was only seen in GOES CCOR-1. The source is most likely a small piece of ejecta seen over the NE limb in SDO AIA 304 starting at 2026-08-02T09:09Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Plane-of-sky measurement chosen due to single view point and beyond-limb source.

data.note: CME observed best to the E in STEREO A COR2. Also observed faintly to the W in SOHO LASCO C2 until a downlink gap begins at 2026-08-03T05:00Z, and faintly to the W in GOES CCOR-1. The source may be gradual field line brightening/opening from AR 14501 (S07W43) lasting approximately 2026-08-03T00:00Z to 2026-08-03T04:00Z in SDO AIA 193/211, likely deflected northeastward with proximity to the large southern polar coronal hole seen facing STEREO A EUVI.

cmeAnalyses.note: Triangulation between STEREO A COR2, SOHO LASCO C2, and GOES CCOR-1. The front is notably more faint in LASCO and CCOR-1.

data.note: CME observed to the NE in only STEREO A COR2, likely pylon obscured in GOES CCOR-1 and unavailable in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 real-time due to a downlink gap. The likely source is AR 14498, observed in SDO AIA 304 first as a filament jostling with surface brightening starting around 2026-08-03T07:10Z, followed by a wider swath of faint dimming and brightening starting around 2026-08-03T08:16Z in SDO AIA 171/193, all centered ~N22W12.

cmeAnalyses.note: STEREO A COR2 only 3D analysis using N22W12 as the approximate source, finding some northward deflection. May be some variance in the parameters without other coronagraph imagery to triangulate.

data.note: An increase above x-ray flux background levels is observed starting at 2026-07-20T19:08Z, but this is to the east of the brightening observed with the M1.1 flare.
Simultaneous flaring from S20E19 and an unnumbered AR on the E limb around N06.
